metric_domain_correction.discovery: The frozen project definition of 'Tiny Recall@90' is the DETECTION criterion (component overlap >= 1 pixel), NOT >=90% component-pixel coverage.

authoritative_source.Tg_definition: GLOBAL_ONLY Tiny Recall@90 = mean over TINY components of (global mask >=1px overlap)

metric_domain_correction.defect_in_asrun_artifact: The as-run artifact's aggregate layer used the strict >=90%-coverage definition, producing a metric-domain mismatch with Tg/G. The pipeline outputs (fused masks and per-component overlap pixels) were correct and are unchanged.
metric_domain_correction.defect_origin: reports/audits/h3_downstream_evaluator_binding.json bound the metric definition as 'downstream_recall90 = overlap/component_pixels>=0.90' (strict coverage). That definition is inconsistent with the earlier-frozen reference Tg = 0.7916666666666666, which is the DETECTION criterion (>=1px overlap) per reports/audits/phase14_clean_v3_global_reference_freeze.json. Using a strict-coverage TinyRecall_H3 against a detection-domain Tg and a detection-domain gap G is a category error: the numerator and denominator are in different metric domains.
metric_domain_correction.why_detection_is_formal: R_H3 = (TinyRecall_H3 - Tg) / G is only meaningful when TinyRecall_H3, Tg, and G share a metric domain. The frozen Tg (0.7916666666666666 = 57/72) and G (0.20833333333333337 = 15/72) are detection-domain quantities, so the formal TinyRecall_H3 must be detection-domain. This is a correctness-driven (not favorability-driven) alignment.
metric_domain_correction.correction_action: Re-aggregate the saved per-component overlap pixels in the frozen detection domain. No inference, no checkpoint change, no pipeline change, no threshold change.

primary_metric_definition.not_the_proposal_coverage: This is a DOWNSTREAM segmentation quantity (post-refiner fusion), not the localizer-only proposal coverage90.

supply_agreement_check.discrepancy: Off-by-one on TINY only (21 vs 22; SMALL/MEDIUM/LARGE agree exactly). Root cause: GT component bbox provenance. The supply-axis evaluator sourced GT bboxes from reports/tables/phase13_predicted_roi_per_component.csv, whereas this downstream evaluator uses extract_gt_components(raw_mask) (the frozen Phase-14 method). One TINY component's bbox is an edge case between the two provenances. The supply gates are already INVALID_FOR_FORMAL_ADJUDICATION and are not used here.

provenance_caveats: The frozen PREDICTED baseline (GLOBAL/PREDICTED/ORACLE contrast rows) was produced by the bound Phase-14 clean-v3 evaluator, whose localizer was constructed WITHOUT an explicit heatmap_resolution (KUBLocalizer default = 512, logit_downsample = Identity).

The H3 downstream arm follows the frozen prospective design, which specifies a 128-space heatmap; the H3 localizer is therefore constructed with heatmap_resolution=128 (logit_downsample = AvgPool2d(4)), which is also the training-faithful construction.

Consequently the frozen PREDICTED contrast row and the H3 row differ in localizer heatmap-decode construction in addition to the localizer checkpoint. This is a provenance nuance of the pre-existing frozen artifacts, NOT introduced by this task. It is recorded here for transparency and is flagged as an unresolved issue.
The proposal-supply agreement check confirms the H3 arm reproduces the previously saved supply metrics (zero-proposal GT=27, TINY=22) exactly.
